verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO harness graded the submitted patch with a continuous reward of 0.852 on the gm_speedup_patch_commit metric and gated pass at reward > 1.20, yielding binary_reward 0 [1][2][3]. The task asked for maximal benchmark speedup while preserving functional equivalence [4], and held-out gso_test_0.py reproduces the prompt's 200k-row contiguous-select workload exactly [5]. The agent did submit a substantive 8812-byte patch touching Dataset.select and formatting/query paths—avoiding list(indices) for ranges, using to_numpy for index maps, and replacing fast_gather with pyarrow take [6][7]—and all thirteen verifier runs passed equivalence checks [7]. On the instruction-matching test 0 the patch cut mean time from ~0.243s to ~0.032s (~7.5×), nearly matching the reference commit's ~0.031s [8], but across the full suite the patch remained slower than the reference commit on most workloads (e.g., test 8 contiguous-select/generator scenarios stayed ~0.747s versus commit ~0.569s) [9], producing an overall geometric-mean commit/patch ratio of 0.852—below both 1.0 and the 1.20 bar [3][9]. The agent declared success from a local benchmark.py run at 0.032s and ignored two failing pytest select tests in its own environment [10][11], so this is TN rather than FN: meaningful progress on one scenario, but not a task-complete optimization at the required threshold.
